item.title: Gustave: Africa's Most Wanted Predator Nobody Can Kill
item.description:
Deep in Burundi's Ruzizi River and the shores of Lake Tanganyika lives a Nile crocodile so large, so old, and so lethal that local legend and scientific record have started to blur. Gustav is estimated at over 18 feet long and 2,000 pounds — a size modern crocodile biology says shouldn't be possible for this population. He's been linked to over 300 human deaths across three decades, yet he's evaded every trap, every hunter, and every expedition sent to capture him.
In this episode, we break down the biology behind why Gustav grew so large, the hunting strategy that's kept him alive for over 60 years, and why researchers believe he may be one of the last of his kind — a predator that time, and the ecosystem collapse around him, should have already erased.
This is Part 1 of the Gustav Files. Part 2 drops next — where we cover the expeditions that came closest to catching him, and why every one of them failed.
